subject: chemistry
title: What changes an equilibrium constant
key_idea: Only a change in temperature changes the value of an equilibrium constant. Changes in concentration, pressure or a catalyst do not. The constant controls the position: any change moves the system until the ratio of products to reactants matches the constant again.

blocks.text: The value of Kc or Kp is fixed at a given temperature. Of everything you can change, only temperature alters it.

diagram.alt: Sort changes into those that alter the value of the equilibrium constant and those that do not.
diagram.prompt: Does the change alter the value of K?

items.text: Increase the concentration of a reactant

items: A catalyst speeds up both directions equally, so K is unchanged.
A change in concentration or pressure shifts the position, but K stays the same once equilibrium is re-established.
Higher temperature increases K for an endothermic reaction and decreases it for an exothermic reaction.

sections.heading: How K controls the position of equilibrium

blocks.text: At equilibrium the ratio of product to reactant terms equals K. Any change that disturbs this ratio makes the system move until the ratio equals K again.

items: Adding a reactant makes the ratio of products to reactants smaller than K.
The reaction moves to the right, making more product, until the ratio is equal to K again.
Removing a product also makes the ratio smaller, so the position moves right.
For N₂O₄ ⇌ 2NO₂, doubling the pressure doubles every partial pressure.
The Kp expression has p(NO₂)² on top, so the ratio becomes larger than Kp.
The position moves left, towards fewer moles of gas, until the ratio equals Kp again.
A change of temperature changes the value of K itself.
For an exothermic reaction, raising the temperature lowers K. The ratio is now above the new K, so the position moves left.
For an endothermic reaction, raising the temperature raises K, so the position moves right.
This explains the effect of temperature on the position in terms of the constant.
A change in concentration or pressure moves the position until the ratio again equals the unchanged K.
A change in temperature changes K, so the position moves to match the new value.

checks.q: State which of temperature, pressure, concentration and a catalyst change the value of Kc.
checks.a: Only temperature changes the value of Kc.

checks.q: The forward reaction is exothermic. State and explain what happens to Kp when the temperature is increased.
checks.a: Kp decreases. Increasing temperature moves the position in the endothermic (reverse) direction, so the proportion of products falls and Kp is smaller.

checks.q: The pressure on a gaseous equilibrium is increased and the position moves to the right. Explain why Kp does not change.
checks.a: Kp depends only on temperature. The partial pressures change until the ratio of terms in the Kp expression is equal to the same value of Kp again.

items: The same principles apply to other equilibrium constants, where appropriate, for example Ka, Kw and Ksp.
Each is constant at a given temperature and changes only when the temperature changes.
